title: fix(app-shell): Studio's Automations pillar honours a read-only package on its Enabled switch and flow inspector (objectui#11124)
body:
Fixes #11124
Clause-②: no

## What was wrong

On a read-only package (a source-loaded package, `writable: false`) the Automations pillar hid "New" and blocked autosave, but two flow-authoring affordances ignored the flag. The header "Enabled" switch stayed clickable: a click saved a flow draft the server refused (`ITEM_LOCKED`), and the switch and the canvas status kept the refused value until the pillar was reopened. The flow inspector was created with a hardcoded `readOnly: false`, so a node edit took on the canvas and was silently discarded. Separately, a refused toggle never rolled back, on any package.

## What changed (`StudioDesignSurface.tsx`, `AutomationsPillar`)

- **Switch.** `disabled` also takes `readOnly`; on a read-only package its title is the existing `engine.studio.pkg.readonlyHint` string (no new i18n key). `toggleEnabled` also returns early on `readOnly`, the same belt-and-braces the Data pillar's `addField` carries.
- **Inspector.** Created with the pillar's real `readOnly`, exactly as the Data pillar threads it (objectui#2259). `FlowInspector` spreads its props into `FlowNodeInspector` / `FlowEdgeInspector`, which already disable every input on `readOnly`, so no inspector file moved.
- **Rollback of a refused toggle.** When the toggle's draft save is refused, `status` is put back to the value the toggle started from, so the switch and the canvas status pill (both read `draft.status`) never show a status the server refused. Only `status` is restored, and only while the draft on screen is still the same flow and still holds the refused status: an edit made while the save was in flight survives, and a refusal that lands after the author opened another flow never rewrites that flow. The dispatch's mechanism note proposed restoring the whole pre-toggle draft; ablation leg E below measures what that would lose.
- **Canvas, a declared bounded in-place fix.** The canvas was handed the pillar's `onPatch`, so on a read-only package it still offered add, insert, drag and delete, each a write thrown away: the card's own symptom on a third affordance. On a read-only package it now gets no `onPatch`, which the preview contract (`MetadataPreviewProps.onPatch`, "When omitted, the preview surface is read-only") reads as read-only. `editing` stays true, so clicking a node or edge still opens the inspector, read-only. The four conditions: (1) same defect class as this card, a flow-authoring affordance ignoring `readOnly`; (2) mechanical, and its shape is the preview registry's documented contract, not a second read-only mechanism; (3) same file as this claim, and no other claim holds it; (4) same gate family, no new verification surface. `FlowPreview.tsx` and `FlowCanvas.tsx` are not touched (objectui#10862 slice 4 holds them).

## Pins (`StudioDesignSurface.automationsReadOnly-11124.test.tsx`)

The canvas and the inspector are the real registered `FlowPreview` and `FlowInspector`; the client is a server double whose draft save can refuse (403 `ITEM_LOCKED`) and can be held open.

- read-only: the switch is disabled, carries the read-only hint, and a click saves nothing;
- read-only: a selected node opens the inspector with its Label and ID inputs disabled;
- read-only: the canvas offers no "Add connected node" or "Insert node here" handle;
- writable, the control: the switch, the inspector and the canvas all still edit, and a toggle saves `status: obsolete`;
- refused toggle: the switch and the canvas status return to `active`, and the server's refusal text is shown;
- refused toggle with an edit in flight: `status` returns, the Label edit survives;
- refused toggle after opening a second flow: the second flow keeps its served status.

## Reverse verification

Fix committed first (`5b92f7ab4`). Each leg went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (objectstack), which asserted anchor 1 to 0 and a changed blob, ran the file, then restored and proved blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty. The subject resolves through a relative source import, not a package `dist/`, so no rebuild step applies. Directions were registered before the run; every leg answered as registered.

| leg | mutation | red | green |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | switch `disabled` without `readOnly` | switch pin (`toBeDisabled`) | other 6 |
| B | inspector `readOnly: false` again | inspector pin (`toBeDisabled`) | other 6 |
| C | canvas handed `onPatch` again | canvas pin (1 "Add connected node" found) | other 6 |
| D | no rollback | refused-toggle pin, in-flight-edit pin | other 5 |
| E | whole-draft rollback, `setDraft(prevDraft)` | in-flight-edit pin, second-flow pin | other 5 |

Its `readOnly` prop documents a narrower scope ("hide/disable nav-authoring affordances"). This is from reading the source only; it was not measured through a public door, is not filed, and is not touched here.
